status_notes: supersedes the prior statement, which used justification vulnerable_code_not_in_execute_path (imprecise: that asserts the code is PRESENT but unreachable). Correct basis is component_not_present, and it is structurally provable: `cargo tree -i yaml-rust --edges normal` returns "nothing to print" — no normal-edge path exists; the only path is yaml-rust <- serde_yaml <- insta [dev-dependencies] <- cargo-vet, and cargo never links dev-dependencies into a release binary. ALSO CORRECTS an inaccurate claim in the prior statement: tool binaries are built with `cargo install`, NOT `cargo auditable build`, so they carry no embedded dependency data — `cargo audit bin` on cargo-vet.exe warns the report is incomplete (81 of ~183 deps recovered by heuristic). That run corroborates absence (yaml-rust/serde_yaml/insta: 0 hits, 0 findings) but is NOT the proof; the cargo dependency-graph structure is.
author: bgonz808

status_notes: MAINTAINER DECISION (2026-08-25): accepted as a false positive. Stated basis: the immediately preceding digests of this same source were clean, and the only change is the addition of hardening flags. Supporting evidence gathered before the decision: 1/70 detections; the six major peer engines checked (BitDefender, Symantec, ESET-NOD32, Kaspersky, Sophos, TrendMicro) all report undetected; times_submitted=1, so there is no in-the-wild prevalence; the artifact carries a verified SLSA provenance attestation from our own producer. The `!ml` suffix denotes a machine-learning heuristic, which Microsoft documents as frequently false-positive on unsigned binaries, and rust-lang/rust#88297 records this same family firing on a plain hello_world rustc build with no hardening involved. HONEST LIMITS: no sandbox verdict was available at decision time, and the hardening-causes-FP hypothesis is NOT established -- four sibling tools built with identical flags stayed 0/70, and binary size does not explain the difference either. This ack covers ONLY this (digest, engine) pair; a new engine or a new digest re-raises.
author: bgonz808

Disabled-mode cackle ran build scripts unwrapped and discarded their stdout, so it never saw cargo: directives; under Bubblewrap ring gains build.allow_build_instructions (its own static libs and link-search path under the runner's target dir); libz-sys gains include=/usr/include and rustc-link-lib=z, i.e. on this LINUX proxy measurement it linked the system zlib dynamically, which the MSVC producer build does not do (libz-sys compiles bundled zlib there) — a known fidelity limit of the Linux-proxy caps axis, recorded, not a grant. No allow_apis grant changed. Measurement method shown reproducible on cargo-deny (second run byte-identical, 42755270577); this tool measured once
